Root cause found & fixed for repeated "Anthropic thinking blocks require signature" ProviderError: assistant `thinking` content blocks produced by non-Anthropic providers (chatgpt, gemini, openai-compatible) never carry a `signature` (it's optional in ThinkingBlockSchema). When a thread switches models mid-conversation (e.g. chatgpt-5.5 -> claude-sonnet-5), replaying that history verbatim made `convertAssistantContentBlock` in packages/core/src/llm/provider/anthropic.ts throw on the old thinking block, permanently poisoning the thread — every subsequent user turn failed identically since the offending history entry never gets removed. Fixed by dropping (returning undefined for) assistant thinking blocks without a signature during Anthropic conversion, mirroring the existing pattern for foreign `provider_tool_use` blocks (see anthropic.ts convertAssistantContentBlock, and test packages/core/test/llm/provider/anthropic.test.ts). Confirmed via session log .diligent/sessions/20260701025515091000-a2bde4.jsonl. Note: persisting the user message before the provider call is normal/intended chat behavior and not the actual bug — the recurring failure was caused by permanently-poisoned history, not premature persistence.

apply_patch semantics observed in this Diligent host and prior Codex source review: Add File overwrites existing files; Move to overwrites an existing destination by writing destination then removing source; Update File with Move to can rename while editing content; Delete File removes files but not now-empty directories. Important: patch application is not atomic for all failures — in a stress test on 2026-07-01, a first successful hunk in file-a.txt remained applied even though a later Update File for a missing file failed. Therefore after any failed apply_patch, inspect actual file state before retrying or assuming rollback. Codex implementation lives under ~/git/codex/codex-rs/apply-patch; parser supports Add File/Delete File/Update File/Move to, and tests cover overwrites and failure-after-partial-success behavior.

Bug fixed: In the web client, completed sub-agents showed status "running" after a page refresh (thread resume). Root cause: on resume the server (packages/runtime/src/app-server/thread-read-builder.ts buildThreadReadItems) emits spawn_agent/wait/close_agent only as generic `toolCall` items (never `collabEvent`), so `applyLiveCollabStatusesToSnapshot` is a no-op on the read path (it only touches collabEvent items, and runtime.agent registry is empty when idle). The web client reconstructs collab cards entirely in packages/web/src/client/lib/thread-hydration.ts by parsing tool outputs: spawn output -> threadId/nickname + status "running"; wait output JSON -> per-agent status used to upgrade the spawn status via setSpawnStatus. The wait tool (packages/runtime/src/collab/wait.ts) embeds each child's FULL output inside `status[id].output`, so the result JSON is often huge and gets tail-truncated by the executor (packages/core/src/tool/executor.ts + truncation.ts, default direction "tail", MAX 50KB). Tail-truncation drops the leading `{"status":...}` header, so JSON.parse fails, no status upgrade happens, and the spawn stays "running". Fix (client-only, thread-hydration.ts): when parseWaitOutput fails, fall back using wait's `input.ids` (small, never truncated) plus statuses recovered from the human-readable `summary` lines (e.g. `"Cleo: Completed — ..."`) which survive in the tail; default to "completed" since wait() only returns after agents finish or time out; preserve errored/still-running fidelity from summary; derive timedOut via /"timed_out":\s*true/ regex. Added parseWaitSummaryStatuses helper (maps Completed->completed, Error->errored, Still running->running, Pending->pending, Shutdown->shutdown). TUI is unaffected because it renders collab by loading the child thread directly rather than tracking a spawn status badge. Regression tests in packages/web/test/client/lib/thread-store.test.ts. Note: a more robust long-term fix would persist collab terminal status as structured session data rather than re-parsing possibly-truncated tool output.

MCP OAuth connect bug (root cause CONFIRMED + fixed 2026-07-01). SYMPTOM: web `/mcp list` showed atlassian green, but at web-server startup the tool-build connect failed: `[mcp] server "atlassian" unavailable: Streamable HTTP error ... {"error":"invalid_token","error_description":"Missing or invalid access token"}`, and after the isNeedsAuth broadening it degraded to `[mcp] server "atlassian" needs authorization — run /mcp login atlassian`. A diagnostic `[mcp:diag]` line printed `connect failed (authProvider=no)`, proving the connect built NO OAuth authProvider → no Bearer token attached → server rejected it → refresh was skipped (the `!authProvider` short-circuit). ROOT CAUSE: OAuth deps (`McpConnectionManager.setOAuthDeps`) were wired ONLY in `createAppServerConfig` (factory.ts), but the startup tool build (buildDefaultTools → createMcpToolProvider → sync → connect) ran BEFORE that wiring (the `[mcp:diag]` line printed before the app-server's own "starting server" log), so `manager.oauthDeps` was undefined at connect time and `connect()` never created `createConnectOAuthProvider`. Standalone `auth(provider,{serverUrl})` refresh worked fine (returns AUTHORIZED, rotates+saves tokens) — proving the token/refresh itself was healthy; the only problem was the missing provider. FIX (packages/runtime/src/tools/defaults.ts): in buildDefaultTools, when mcpServers are present, guarantee deps on the exact singleton the provider will sync — `const m = getMcpManager(); if (!m.hasOAuthDeps()) m.setOAuthDeps({ storeDir: join(dirname(getGlobalConfigPath()), "mcp-oauth"), openBrowser })` BEFORE pushing createMcpToolProvider. Added `McpConnectionManager.hasOAuthDeps()` guard so a later richer app-server opener is never clobbered. This fixes ordering AND any manager-instance mismatch because defaults.ts and provider.ts both reach the same relative `./mcp/client` singleton. RELATED prior fixes in client.ts (same session): (1) isNeedsAuth() regex broadened to invalid_token|invalid_grant|missing or invalid access token|token expired|403 so such failures classify as needs_auth not hard error; (2) connect() silent refresh+retry via injectable authRefresh (SDK `auth`, default) — on needs_auth-classified failure with an authProvider, force refresh_token grant (no browser; connect provider throws NeedsAuthError on redirect) then reconnect once via a FRESH client (openConnection helper; reusing a Client after a failed connect is unreliable). Tests: runtime/test/tools/defaults.test.ts asserts buildDefaultTools sets hasOAuthDeps when mcpServers present (injected in-memory manager); runtime/test/tools/mcp/client.test.ts covers invalid_token->needs_auth, silent-refresh-then-reconnect, refresh-cannot-authorize->needs_auth. `[mcp:diag]` tracing is gated behind DILIGENT_DEBUG_MCP=1. NOTE: @diligent/runtime resolves to SOURCE (packages/runtime/src via package.json exports, no dist) so src edits take effect immediately with `bun run`. Still worth manual-verifying the real web startup now shows atlassian connected (green, no error) after this fix.

MCP needs_auth is now surfaced to the agent via the system prompt (implemented 2026-07-01, Option B chosen over an agent-drivable synthetic login tool). WHY B over A: a synthetic `mcp__<server>__login` tool that the agent drives is worse right now because (1) logging in mid-turn does not expose the real server tools in the same agent instance — tools are fixed at agent-build time (buildDefaultTools -> MCP sync) and live tools/list_changed refresh is still backlog; in-memory resume reuses existing agent/tools; (2) login opens the browser SERVER-SIDE with a loopback callback on the app-server, so remote app-server can't complete it; (3) agent auto-initiating auth is a surprise/security concern. A becomes viable only after live tool-list refresh + client-side browser open exist. IMPLEMENTATION: pure helper buildMcpNeedsAuthNote(statuses: McpServerStatus[]): string|undefined in packages/runtime/src/tools/mcp/needs-auth-note.ts (exported from tools/mcp/index.ts) — filters status==="needs_auth", returns a note listing each with "run `/mcp login <name>`" plus an instruction to NOT attempt those tools; returns undefined when none. WIRED in packages/runtime/src/app-server/factory.ts createRuntimeAgent via new async appendMcpNeedsAuthNote(systemPrompt, mcpServers): called AFTER buildDefaultTools (so getMcpManager().listStatus reads the authoritative cached sync result set with OAuth deps already configured by createAppServerConfig; listStatus does not reconnect since lastStatus is already populated), appends a SystemSection {tag:"mcp_status", label:"mcp_needs_auth", cacheControl:"ephemeral"} before applyModeToPrompt. KEY INSIGHT the user drove: auth state cannot be known from any local flag/token-file alone — only the connect attempt result (McpConnectionManager.sync -> isNeedsAuth on NeedsAuthError/401/403/invalid_token/etc., cached in lastStatus, surfaced by listStatus) is authoritative; a stored token file can be stale (Atlassian returns invalid_token on a non-401 body). Tests: packages/runtime/test/tools/mcp/needs-auth-note.test.ts. NOTE on the earlier Claude comparison: the `authenticate`/`complete_authentication` "tools" seen in Claude are NOT the official Atlassian Rovo server's MCP tools — the official server uses transport-layer OAuth 2.1 (browser consent -> Bearer token in Authorization header) and exposes only product tools (Jira/Confluence read/write/search); those auth "tools" are Claude's host/connector-layer representation of the OAuth flow. So "connect anonymously and let the server present auth tools" does not work for the official Atlassian server.

[discovery] MCP lazy tool loading ("tool search") IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-01 (proxy approach; the earlier "context grows linearly" gap vs Claude Code is now addressed). DESIGN DECISION: Diligent's agent tool set is FIXED at agent-build time (packages/core/src/agent/agent.ts stores tools[]; loop.ts rebuilds registry per turn from the immutable config.tools; assistant.ts toFunctionToolDefinition serializes every tool each turn) — there is NO dynamic mid-conversation tool registration and no meta/deferred-tool mechanism. So codex-rs's native approach (ToolSpec::ToolSearch single `tool_search` tool + `defer_loading=true`/`output_schema=None` via OpenAI Responses API, execution loaded natively) is NOT portable (we are multi-provider). Chosen instead: a self-contained PROXY surface (no core surgery). User steer: keep proxy execution (declined dynamic-registration option B), and do NOT cram search+call into one action-discriminated tool — use codex-like SPLIT: a dedicated search tool + a separate run tool. IMPLEMENTATION (all in packages/runtime/src/tools/mcp/): (1) tool-search.ts: createMcpSearchTool(catalog) -> tool `mcp_search_tools` {query?,server?} returns matched entries {server,tool,description(≤400),inputSchema} as JSON, token-overlap scoring, MAX_SEARCH_RESULTS=25 with "Showing N of M" note, and a compact `server (n): tool1, tool2` index baked into the tool DESCRIPTION so names load upfront (schemas deferred); createMcpRunTool({catalog,manager,host}) -> tool `mcp_run_tool` {server,tool,args?} validates (server\0tool) against catalog Set then proxies. (2) to-tool.ts: extracted shared mapMcpCallResult() + callMcpToolWithApproval() (approval + manager.call + result map) reused by BOTH the eager per-tool bridge and the run proxy. (3) types.ts: McpCatalogEntry, McpToolLoading, DEFAULT_MCP_LAZY_THRESHOLD=20. (4) provider.ts: createMcpToolProvider(servers, {toolLoading?, lazyThreshold?}) builds a catalog after sync (per-tool toggles applied), resolveLoading() maps auto->eager|lazy by catalog.length>threshold; eager returns mcp__server__tool per tool, lazy returns [mcp_search_tools, mcp_run_tool], empty catalog returns []. CONFIG: new top-level `mcp` object in config/schema.ts (McpGlobalConfigSchema: toolLoading enum auto|eager|lazy, lazyThreshold int). WIRING: buildDefaultTools gained mcpToolLoading (DEFAULT "eager") + mcpLazyThreshold, passed to createMcpToolProvider; ONLY factory.ts createRuntimeAgent passes the real value (runtimeConfig.diligent.mcp?.toolLoading ?? "auto") so the runtime agent goes auto/lazy; tool-handlers.ts (tool settings/catalog surface) intentionally omits it -> stays EAGER so per-tool toggles remain visible in settings UI. Exports added to mcp/index.ts. Docs: docs/guide/mcp-servers.md "Tool loading (eager vs lazy)" section. Tests: runtime/test/tools/mcp/tool-search.test.ts (search index/filter/scope/no-match/limit; run valid/invalid) + provider.test.ts lazy/auto-below/auto-above/empty-lazy cases. 370 tools+app-server tests pass; tsc+biome clean. LIMITATION vs codex: proxy loses provider-native function-schema validation for the actual call (args validated server-side; schema shown via search). A future "real dynamic tool registration" (mutable per-turn tool set) would unify this with tools/list_changed refresh + skill runtime reload + thread fork and give native calling — deferred as a separate larger initiative. NOTE: /reload rebuilds config+restarts app-server (config-manager.ts reloadConfig) so it refreshes the lazy catalog for free, but reload is coarse (full restart, between-turns) and still eager per rebuild — it does NOT itself reduce per-turn context; lazy loading is the orthogonal fix.

Root cause found & fixed (2026-07-02) for ProviderError 400 "messages.N: `tool_use` ids were found without `tool_result` blocks immediately after" (Anthropic) that occurs after the user ABORTS a tool mid-execution and then sends a new message. Session 20260702040251285000-7c601b reproduced it: bash tool aborted -> tool_result "[Aborted by user]" WAS persisted in the session tree (via tool_end event staging), yet the next request still sent an orphaned tool_use. KEY INSIGHT: the persisted session tree and the CACHED AGENT'S IN-MEMORY conversation are two separate things. turn-orchestrator caches the agent (this._agent) and only re-seeds its conversation from persisted history once (`if (agent !== this._initializedAgent)`), so subsequent prompts send the agent's own in-memory conversation, NOT the (valid, repaired) persisted tree. In packages/core/src/agent/loop.ts the tool-result push was guarded by `if (!signal.aborted) conversation.push(execution.toolResult)`, so on abort the executed tool's result was emitted as tool_end (persisted) but DROPPED from the agent's in-memory conversation, leaving assistant(tool_use) with no following tool_result -> next request 400s, permanently until restart/resume (resume rebuilds context from the valid tree). FIX: (1) loop.ts now ALWAYS pushes every execution.toolResult to conversation regardless of abort. (2) packages/core/src/agent/tool.ts runToolCalls gained fillAbortedExecutions(): on abort, synthesizes a "[Aborted by user]" tool_result (emitting tool_start if not already + tool_end) for every tool_call that never executed (parallel: results dropped after the first break; sequential: later calls never start), so BOTH conversation and persisted tree keep every tool_use paired. Parallel path passes allStarted=true (tool_start already emitted upfront); sequential passes false. Note: runtime SessionManager.repairEntries() only fixes the PERSISTED tree (when the last path entry is an assistant with unmatched tool_calls) and cannot fix the cached agent's in-memory conversation — that's why the core-loop fix is required. Tests: packages/core/test/agent/loop.test.ts ("aborted single tool: result stays in conversation" + updated "parallel abort" now expects 2 tool_end + tc_1/tc_2 tool_results). tsc + biome clean.

Issue #217 analysis (2026-07-02): ToolResult.metadata exists at execution boundary but is collapsed before persistence/protocol. Flow: Tool.execute returns ToolResult.metadata (packages/core/src/tool/types.ts); executeTool preserves/enriches it for internal result (e.g. error/truncated). runToolCalls -> toToolCallExecution (packages/core/src/agent/tool.ts) creates ToolResultMessage with output/outputImages/render and `isError: !!result.metadata?.error`, dropping the rest of metadata and any potential status. CoreAgentEvent tool_end also has only output/outputImages/isError/render (packages/core/src/agent/types.ts). Protocol schemas mirror that: ToolResultMessageSchema, AgentEvent tool_end, and ThreadItem toolCall have no metadata/status carrier (packages/protocol/src/data-model.ts). Runtime TurnStager rebuilds persisted tool_result from tool_end, so session JSONL cannot retain metadata (packages/runtime/src/session/turn-stager.ts). thread/read snapshots also expose only output/outputImages/isError/render (packages/runtime/src/app-server/thread-read-builder.ts). Provider-facing LLM conversion is separate: Anthropic/OpenAI/Gemini still send the text output (and Anthropic sends is_error); the LLM is NOT receiving only isError. The real bug is that structured machine-readable status (validation issue counts, partial mutation, retry/readback hints, truncation fullOutputPath, etc.) is lost for persistence/protocol/client/audit and for future turns unless encoded into prose output. Fix should add a structured carrier (metadata and/or narrowed status) through ToolResultMessage, CoreAgentEvent tool_end/turn_end, protocol ThreadItem, runtime staging/read, and reducers, while keeping arbitrary metadata out of provider request payloads unless explicitly intended.

Web `/reload` parity with CLI TUI's `/reload` implemented (2026-07-02). BACKGROUND: TUI's `/reload` works by respawning its whole app-server child process (packages/cli/src/tui/app.ts restartRpcClient), which forces packages/runtime/src/config/runtime.ts loadRuntimeConfig to re-run discoverSkills/discoverAgents/buildDefaultTools(mcpServers) from scratch — full parity confirmed via earlier session. Web's server (packages/web/src/server/index.ts) is a long-lived shared process (many threads/connections) that can't be restarted per-client, so it had no reload capability at all.
IMPLEMENTATION (shared runtime capability, works for BOTH Web and CLI's stdio app-server since both go through createAppServerConfig):
- New protocol method `config/reload` (DILIGENT_CLIENT_REQUEST_METHODS.CONFIG_RELOAD in packages/protocol/src/methods.ts) with ConfigReloadParamsSchema `{}` and ConfigReloadResponseSchema `{ skills: SkillInfo[] }` in client-requests.ts, wired into both DiligentClientRequestSchema/DiligentClientResponseSchema discriminated unions.
- packages/runtime/src/app-server/factory.ts: createAppServerConfig() assigns `config.reloadConfig` (a new DiligentAppServerConfig field) AFTER the config object literal is built (avoids TDZ). It calls `loadRuntimeConfig(cwd, paths)` fresh and mutates the SAME shared `runtimeConfig` object's mutable fields in place (skills, agents, agentDefinitions, systemPrompt — needed because skill/agent text is baked into systemPrompt at loadRuntimeConfig time via buildSystemPromptWithKnowledge; diligent — the whole config which carries mcpServers/tools/hooks; sources). It ALSO updates the frozen `DiligentAppServerConfig` snapshot fields that createRuntimeAgent/handlers read via `this.config.X` rather than live from runtimeConfig: `config.mcpServers` (used by /mcp list|login|logout via getMcpServers), `config.skillNames` (turn/start slash-command disambiguation), `config.hooks` (Stop/UserPromptSubmit lifecycle hooks). Deliberately did NOT touch providerManager/streamFunction/authStore/permissionEngine/compaction/mode — out of scope for "mcp/tool/skill/agent reload" and carries auth/connection disruption risk; MCP OAuth deps don't need re-wiring since packages/runtime/src/tools/defaults.ts buildDefaultTools already lazily guarantees them via manager.hasOAuthDeps() guard.
- packages/runtime/src/app-server/config-handlers.ts: new `handleConfigReload(reloadConfig, threads: Map<string, ThreadRuntime>)` — throws -32601 "Config reload is not supported by this app server" when hook is undefined (CLI/Web both actually implement it via factory.ts, so this only fires if a future custom host omits it); otherwise calls reloadConfig() then sets `runtime.agent = undefined` for EVERY thread in the map (same "force rebuild on next turn" pattern already used by handleModeSet/turn-handlers' model-override path), so already-open threads pick up fresh skills/agents/tools/mcp on their NEXT turn without disrupting any turn currently in flight.
- Wired through ClientRequestDispatchContext.reloadConfig (request-dispatcher.ts) and DiligentAppServer.buildRequestDispatchContext() (server.ts) reading `this.config.reloadConfig`. New DiligentAppServerConfig.reloadConfig field.
- Web client: added "reload" to BUILTIN_COMMANDS (packages/web/src/client/lib/slash-commands.ts) and a `case "reload"` in useAppActions' handleSlashCommand (packages/web/src/client/lib/use-app-actions.ts) that calls rpc.request(CONFIG_RELOAD, {}) and on success calls the newly-threaded `setSkills(result.skills)` prop (plumbed from use-app-state.ts) so the skill-derived slash command list refreshes client-side too; shows an info toast on success/failure.
